title: The Drowned Wolf
premise: When the valley's border wards collapse on the same night the stars vanish, scribe Freya Sterling learns the wards were powered by a soul sold to the Undercourt beneath the mountain—and that the debt-bond on her own name is a forgery written by the temple's high canon to hide his theft. Freya descends with a disgraced ward-smith, Ash, and a debt-collector's ledger that can rewrite bargains, discovering the Undercourt's drowned king trades in stolen names. To restore the stars she must reclaim the sold soul, which means outbidding the king with the only currency she has left: her own true name, surrendered willingly. In the climax Freya rewrites the ledger to bind the king to his own bargains, freeing the soul and igniting the last dragon-fire; she returns not as a scribe but as the valley's new keeper of wards, choosing a belonging she once fled.
about_author: Mirabel Sandoval is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging medieval debt contracts, an obsession that seeps into her tales of bargains and borrowed names. She writes from a coastal cottage where, she insists, the tide keeps better secrets than she does.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Freya, copying tithes in the temple's cold scriptorium, feels the wards fail as every star vanishes overhead. The high canon orders silence, but Freya finds her own name missing from the debt rolls—a gap no honest ledger has. Fear and a flicker of forbidden curiosity drive her to steal the roll. Beat: the shattering of a carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The stolen roll reveals her bond was forged in a hand she recognizes: the canon's. Confronting him, she's accused of theft and sentenced to ward-repair duty at the border—the one place magic cannot follow. Ash, the exiled ward-smith, watches her go with knowing eyes. Beat: betrayal by an institution she served faithfully.

chapters.title: Where Magic Ends
chapters.summary: Freya's POV at the dead border, where Ash catches up and reveals the wards were never powered by prayer but by a soul sold to the Undercourt—and the sale contract bears Freya's family name. The stars went out because the soul is dying. Beat: reluctant alliance; the first step past safety into consequence.

chapters.title: The Debt-Collector's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. He leads Freya to a drowned shrine where a dead collector's ledger lies—ink that can rewrite any bargain, at a price paid in memory. Freya pays a memory of her mother to claim it. Beat: the theme of survival's price made literal; power acquired through loss.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The two enter the mountain's flooded throat, navigating bargains with river-things who demand riddles of true names. Freya lies for the first time in her life and feels something in her change. Beat: corruption's first taste; the valley's innocence left behind.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Undercourt: a drowned cathedral of chained dragon-fire, courtiers wearing stolen faces, and the drowned king holding the sold soul in a lantern of bone. He recognizes the ledger and offers Freya a seat at his table. Beat: temptation—power offered freely, which is the most dangerous kind.

chapters.title: What the King Bought
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The soul is Ash's sister's—his exile was the price of her sale, and his guilt is the reason the wards failed: he stopped maintaining a lie. Freya's anger at his concealment nearly breaks the alliance. Beat: midpoint rupture; belonging tested by honesty.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Drowned
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. To free the soul she must outbid the king, and the ledger demands her true name—the self that survives all rewriting. She begins drafting the bargain, discovering the king's own contracts contain a flaw: he never named himself. Beat: the plan crystallizes; dread and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, climax. At the court's heart she rewrites the ledger, binding the king to every bargain he ever made—his own unnamed soul forfeit to his rules. The dragon-fire roars free, stars reignite overhead, and Ash's sister wakes. Freya, nameless and shaking, chooses a new name aloud: keeper. Beat: triumph purchased with self-erasure, then self-authorship.

chapters.title: A New Name for the Valley
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, resolution. The valley's people, starlit again, must decide who guards the wards; the canon falls, and Freya—no longer scribe, no longer debt-bound—accepts keeper's office with Ash beside her. The ledger is sealed beneath the mountain. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned; power held with memory of its cost.
